concerns.concern: The half-integer flux intercept, read as a π phase from opposite-chirality d ± id order, could instead come from trapped Abrikosov vortices shifting the Josephson phase. The half-integer values spread from about 0.75π to 0.95π, depend on sweep direction, and the period is about seven times smaller than Φ0/Ageo, suggesting flux in nearby flakes couples to the loop. A zero-field-cooled repeat at each in-plane field is requested.
concerns.quote: Warm above Tc, cool in zero field, and repeat the Fig. 3 intercept at each in-plane value; give intercept error bars

concerns.concern: The intercepts in Fig. 3 and Extended Data Fig. 2 have no stated uncertainty. The Fig. 3a fit spans 41 to 59 µA but is extrapolated to I = 0 over more than twice that span. The slopes differ between 0 and 10 µT in-plane field with no explanation of why A·Lgeo would change, and it is unclear whether each point tracks the same minimum.
concerns.quote: The fit in Fig. 3a spans 41 to 59 µA and extrapolates to I = 0 over more than twice that span

concerns.concern: The number of devices that show each claimed signal is not reported. These signals are the half-period intercept, a finite η′ at B = 0, and the second harmonic. The review also asks why other devices were set aside for the phase measurement and whether any device shows only integer intercepts.
concerns.quote: How many SQUIDs did you fabricate and measure, and in how many did you see a half-period intercept, a finite η′ at B = 0, and the second harmonic?

concerns.concern: In the PDF, the phase result rests on a single 45° device. The other-device data (SI 14) is not available, so a second-best phase dataset should be shown.
concerns.quote: in the PDF the phase result comes from one 45° device

concerns.concern: The finite diode efficiency at zero field, read as broken time-reversal symmetry, could come from a trapped-vortex stray field combined with nonuniform bias, or from a flux offset. In Fig. 4a the Is+(+B) and |Is−(−B)| traces look like copies shifted along B. The authors should measure the residual field and offset, and repeat after zero-field cooling and with swapped current contacts.
concerns.quote: in Fig. 4a the two traces look like copies shifted along B

concerns.concern: The 0° control device, cited as showing no zero-field diode effect, has its data only in the missing SI. Its η′(B) should be plotted alongside Figs. 4a and 4b at matched temperature and bias.
concerns.quote: Plot the 0° device's η′(B) beside Fig. 4a and 4b at matched temperature and bias

concerns.concern: The second harmonic in Is(B), read as Cooper pair co-tunneling, could be a readout distortion of an asymmetric SQUID with comparable geometric and Josephson inductances. Fig. 4c shows cusp-like maxima, so a purely first-harmonic simulation with 3:1 asymmetry and β ∼ 1 should be compared with Fig. 4d.
concerns.quote: Simulate Is(Φ) for a first-harmonic CPR with 3:1 asymmetry and β ∼ 1, and compare its FFT with Fig. 4d

concerns.concern: The background subtraction applied in Fig. 4d is not described, and the review asks how the background was chosen.
concerns.quote: the background subtraction in Fig. 4d is not described

concerns.concern: The full parameter ranges are not disclosed and the chosen ranges are not justified. This covers in-plane fields, perpendicular field ranges, bias currents and temperatures. It is also unclear whether the in-plane sweeps were repeated in another cooldown.
concerns.quote: the reasons for this range and for the bias ranges in Fig. 3 are not given

concerns.concern: The supplementary information (SI 1 to SI 14) is cited throughout but is not included in the v1 PDF, so key supporting material cannot be checked.
concerns.quote: The SI (SI 1 to SI 14) is cited throughout but is not in the v1 PDF

concerns.concern: The paper has no data or code availability statement.
concerns.quote: the PDF has no data or code statement
